lots.guide_summary: All evidence is SOLD or UNSOLD auction results in AUD (rate 1, premium status unknown). No painting is the same work (it is a unique original). Close watercolours with Tasmanian water or harbour subjects run from AUD 220 (Leonard Joel Melbourne 2024, a 1952 dated work, just outside 24 months) to AUD 1,700 (Colville 2026). The two close Hobart sales within 24 months are AUD 800 and AUD 1,700. Category-guide Hobart sales within 24 months are AUD 500-1,400, and Melbourne sales AUD 200-220. UNSOLD last bids are AUD 100-400. No ASKING prices were found.
lots.working: This follows the precedent set for other unique paintings in this run: close same-artist, same-medium SOLD works within 24 months stand in for 'same item'. Keep: lowest close SOLD within 24 months = Colville AUD 800 (11 Feb 2025); 800 / 1.198 = 667.8, round down = $665 (all-in $796.67). Flip: likely resale about AUD 800 back through Colville in Hobart (taking the lower of the two close results, and ignoring the AUD 1,700 outlier), less an assumed 20% vendor cost (commission plus photography and insurance, AUD 160) and $0 postage (local drop-off) = 640; 640 / 2.396 = 267.1, round down = $265. The current bid is $120 (3 bids at 11:05 on 30 Sep 2026), which is $143.76 all-in. Caution: Leonard Joel sold a similar-sized 1952 dated watercolour for only AUD 220 in June 2024, so the Hobart premium is what the bids rest on.
lots.confidence_reason: The signature 'MAX ANGUS 1947' is read clearly (enlarged crop), and 2 close Hobart SOLD results within 24 months were opened in the Invaluable JSON. It is not High because no result is the same work, the individual lot pages were not opened, premium status is unknown and the paper condition is hidden under glass.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the MutualArt 'ASKING' entry: it held no price, was snippet only, and is not an asking price. The Artrecord and MutualArt record figures in its note were snippet only and unverified. All other Invaluable figures were re-checked against the parsed JSON (120 hits) and match. Moved the June 2024 Leonard Joel 1952 result out of the bid calculation because it is just over 24 months old (it is still listed as a caution).
lots.key_photo_findings: Signature and date 'MAX ANGUS 1947' in black lower right, confirmed in an enlarged crop. A two-masted ketch with detailed rigging, working boats, lit windows and a red light across the water, and Mount Wellington behind, consistent with Victoria Dock, Hobart. The colours look fresh. It is in a wide cream mount and a thin ornate gilt frame under glass.
lots.condition: No visible foxing, tears or fading in the photos. The sheet edges and back are hidden, so toning under the mount is unknown.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is 23 x 35 cm the sight size? Are there any labels or inscriptions on the back (title, exhibition, gallery)? Is there any foxing, toning or mould on the sheet under the mount?
